title: Koko Eating Bananas
description: Binary search the ANSWER on [1, max(piles)]: find the minimum k such that `canFinish(k)` is true.

notes: You're binary-searching the answer space, not an index in piles. The predicate `canFinish(k)` is monotonic: false for small k, true for large k.
Use the half-open pattern `while (l < r)` with `r = m` on success and `l = m + 1` on failure — converges on the leftmost true.
`Math.ceil(p / k)` is correct: any leftover banana in a pile costs a whole hour.

options: An index into the piles array
The answer space: candidate eating speeds k from 1..max(piles)

questions.q: Why does this work — what property must the predicate have?
options: It must be monotonic: once k is fast enough, every larger k also works
A partial pile still takes a full hour to finish
JavaScript division returns float; ceil avoids precision bugs only
It doesn't matter for the result

blanks.hint: round up — partial pile still costs an hour
keep m as a candidate when it works

L3.prompt: Write `minEatingSpeed(piles, h)` returning the minimum k bananas/hour Koko needs to finish all piles in h hours. Log `minEatingSpeed([30, 11, 23, 4, 20], 6)`.
hints: Predicate canFinish(k) sums Math.ceil(p / k) and checks <= h.
